title: Blood That Speaks a Better Word
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Abel's blood cried out for justice. The blood of Jesus speaks mercy, forgiveness and peace over sinners.
exhortation: What is this better word that the blood of Jesus speaks over us? First, look at what it doesn't say. Look at the blood of Abel. In Genesis 4:10 the Lord says to Cain, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying to me from the ground."

Can you imagine that cry? A righteous, innocent man murdered by his own brother, his blood soaking into the earth. That blood has a voice. It rises from the ground and cries to God for justice, for vengeance, for a reckoning against the one who spilled it. That is what the blood of Abel says.

Now look at the blood of Jesus: infinitely more precious than Abel's, more righteous, more innocent. And when his blood cries out from the cross, it doesn't cry what Abel's did. It doesn't call for judgment, vengeance or death. It cries for mercy. It speaks forgiveness over us. It speaks peace where Abel's blood spoke judgment, and friendship where Abel's blood spoke condemnation. It speaks steadfast, unshakable love for you and me, sinners who deserve the very cry Abel's blood cried out.
This is who we worship this morning: Jesus, the Son of God, who shed his blood. Not blood that accuses us, but blood that pleads for us.
prayer: Jesus, we thank you for the blood that speaks a better word. There was no other way to drain the cup except that you drink it. You went willingly to the cross to shed your precious blood, the only covering for our sin that could truly forgive.
And you gave yourself. Thank you, Jesus. Amen.
